prompt:
Continue this exact laparoscopic cholecystectomy footage for 10 seconds. Same camera, viewpoint, lighting, colours, image quality and anatomy as the input image.

What is in the scene (taken from the real frame):
A circular laparoscopic view shows the gallbladder on the left and the reddish-brown liver lobe on the right. A metallic surgical grasper with a black insulated shaft enters from the top center, gripping and pulling up the pale pink peritoneal fold near the gallbladder wall. The gallbladder displays a bluish-white surface covered in fine red blood vessels and yellow fatty tissue. Below the grasper, a dissected window reveals two pale tubular structures, with a single silver metallic surgical clip already clamped onto the upper vessel. A small amount of dark red blood coats the tissue immediately beneath the clipped vessel and pools slightly in the lower cavity. No electrocautery hook, no clip applier, and no surgical smoke are present in the scene.

One surgical step happens (chosen by a patient world model): Laparoscopic scissors on a long straight shaft comes into view along its shaft (or, if it is already in view, moves to the cystic duct). It cuts across the cystic duct between the clips.

Instruments already in view: the grasper. An instrument never changes into another instrument. Before the scissors arrives, any instrument in its way slides straight back out of view along its own shaft; the others stay where they are.

By the end of the clip: the cystic duct is divided between its clips.

Motion: slow, small, physically plausible movements only. The camera stays at the same distance and angle with very slight handheld drift. Instruments keep their exact shape, colour, size and entry side. Tissue moves only where an instrument touches it, deforms slightly and springs back.

Keep identical to the input image for the whole clip: the colours, the lighting, the image grain and sharpness, the circular endoscope vignette, and every anatomical structure not named above.

Strictly forbidden: new, extra, swapped or reshaped instruments; a new sac or organ appearing; smoke; zooms, camera cuts or jumps; text or overlays; changes of colour, exposure or image quality; human hands; bleeding; clips.
explanation: Dividing the clipped cystic duct after achieving the critical view of safety proceeds without structural injury, though pre-existing bleeding persists as observed in VID35_01370. Because the cystic artery is already clipped but uncut, the most likely next step is cutting the cystic artery (VID35_01370, VID26_00868) or adjusting gallbladder retraction (VID110_00957), unlike cases where the artery was already divided and dissection began immediately (VID49_00523, VID75_00553).
agent_reason: Both the cystic duct and artery have been clipped twice, so cutting the cystic duct is the next required step in the clipping-and-cutting phase.
